(1) The respective amounts for the subject month and
(2) The respective year-to-date amounts accumulated through the end of the subject month.
(g) The budgeted revenue amounts and budgeted expenditure amounts for the year shall be provided.
(h) Revenue amounts shall be provided by category (e.g., taxes) and by sub-categories (e.g., type of tax).
(i) The finance department shall distribute the monthly consolidated budget reports to the chairperson, the district commissioners and any designees of the chairperson.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
236:
(a) In accordance with this section, the finance department shall prepare and maintain monthly departmental budget reports regarding the respective finances of constitutional offices, offices of other elected officials, appointed boards and county departments operating under the span-of-control of the board of commissioners.
(b) Each monthly departmental budget report shall be a statement of revenues and expenditures for each department prepared in accordance with section 3-43.
(c) The finance department shall distribute each respective monthly departmental budget report to the applicable constitutional officer, elected official, chairperson of an appointed board or head of a county department operating under the span-of-control of the board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
237:
(a) The finance department shall prepare, maintain and distribute annual five-year capital project plans ("ACPP").
(b) Each ACPP shall include projected expenditures for anticipated capital projects for each included year of a rolling five-year period.
(c) Capital projects constitute the acquisition or improvement of capital items with a value in excess of $5,000.00 and with a useful life of at least one year.
(d) Capital items include land, buildings, structures, infrastructure, vehicles, equipment and technology systems.
(e) Expenditures include incurred costs and obligated costs for asset acquisition, contractors, labor, materials, architectural services, engineering services and professional studies.
(f) Each ACPP shall identify the anticipated source(s) of funds for each capital project.

(i) The finance department shall distribute each final ACPP to the chairperson, the district commissioners and any designees of the chairperson.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
238:

(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
241:
This article shall be applicable to the administration of the annual budgeting process of the county.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
242:
(a) The chairperson shall serve as the county's budget officer.
(b) The chairperson as budget officer shall prepare and submit annually to the board of commissioners a proposed budget governing expenditure of all county funds, including capital outlay and public works projects for the following fiscal year pursuant to applicable requirements imposed by Georgia law.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
243:
(a) The county's budget shall include all budgeted funds as approved by the board of commissioners and as administered by the chairperson.

244:

(c) Each budget calendar shall include specific dates for completion of each task necessary to prepare and approve the county's operating budget.
(d) Each budget calendar shall establish the date to have a completed budget approved and adopted.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
245:

(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
246:

247:

(b) Revenues are recognized when they can be measured and become available.
(c) Expenditures are charged when they can be measured, have been incurred and the corresponding liabilities become due.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
248:

249:

250:
In accordance with the provisions of article V, the county may use fund balance exceeding the minimum unrestricted general fund balance of two months as a funding source for the general fund budget.

251:
(a) In each annual budget, the county shall adequately fund its contribution to the defined contribution plan by making, at a minimum, the required contribution.

(b) The county shall strive to make the recommended contribution in lieu of the required contribution.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
254:
This article shall be applicable to the administration of the general fund balance by the county.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
255:
The county shall maintain a minimum unrestricted general fund balance of two months of the previous year's operational expenditures thereby comporting with the Government Finance Officers Association's guidelines of two months of operational expenses.

256:
(a) If necessary, the county may use fund balance exceeding the minimum unrestricted general fund balance of two months as a funding source for the general fund budget.

(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
259:
This article shall be applicable to the generation and administration of revenue by the county.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
260:
(a) The county shall maintain a diversified and stable portfolio of revenue sources.

(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
262:
(a) Conservative revenue projections shall be used for the proposed budget and long-term planning to produce realistic and prudent outcomes.
(b) Such revenue projections shall consider federal, Georgia and local economic data.
(c) Such revenue projections shall consider the performance of each source of revenue historically for at least the previous three fiscal years.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
264:
(a) The grant approval protocols set forth in this section govern the pursuit, development and approval of grant opportunities available to the county which operates under the span-of-control of the board of commissioners.
(b) The pursuit of grant opportunities shall meet the following requirements:
(1) The pursuit of any grant opportunity must be approved in advance by the chairperson and shall be pursued if he or she deems the grant opportunity to be beneficial and otherwise feasible to pursue given the significance and relevance of a grant award, the likelihood of its award and the availability of relevant county's resources to pursue the grant.
(2) The particular county department ("grantee department") that would benefit from the award of proceeds from any grant or any other applicable party shall be responsible for managing the pursuit of any applicable grant
(3) All grant applications must be signed by the chairperson.
(4) The finance department must be informed of grants applied for by the county to assure that accounting procedures are in place to allow expenditure and receipt of grant funds.
(c) The acceptance of grants shall meet the following requirements:
(1) The acceptance of all grants must be approved by the board of commissioners.
(2) All grant agreements must be signed by the chairperson.
(3) The finance department must be informed of grants awarded to the county to assure that accounting procedures are in place to allow expenditure and receipt of grant funds.
(4) Amendments to applicable fund budgets to account for the receipt of the proceeds from any grants must be approved by the board of commissioners.
(d) The utilization of grant proceeds shall meet the following requirements:
(1) The county's procurement approval protocols set forth in article VIII must be followed for all purchases made from grant proceeds, unless the grant conditions state otherwise.
(2) Procurement requests must contain the applicable grant name and number to ensure that the purchase is being charged to the correct grant account.
(3) Copies of the following documents should be provided to the finance department:
• Reimbursement requests when initiated;
• Any amendments to the grant;
• Documentation of reporting requirements and frequency; and
• Any applicable contracts and renewal letters for contractors.
(4) The applicable grantee department is responsible for enforcing the terms and conditions outlined in the applicable grant.
(e) The closeout of any grant shall meet the following requirements:
(1) At the appropriate time, the grantee department must close out the applicable grant pursuant to that grant's closeout standards.
(2) Copies of the final grant report should be submitted to the chairperson, the county clerk and the finance department.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
265:
(a) The county shall aggressively and consistently collect amounts owed to it in a manner consistent with federal, Georgia and local laws so that its revenues will materialize in accordance with its budgets.
(b) Applicable penalties and interest shall be charged on delinquent payments.
(c) The county shall utilize its enforcement capabilities to the fullest possible extent and shall utilize all available legal means of debt collection in a timely manner to collect amounts owed to it in order to ensure budget integrity and minimize lost revenues.
(d) Should the chairperson determine that collection costs may exceed the value of an item subject to collection, the chairperson shall have the discretion to waive the collection requirements imposed by this article.
268:
This article shall be applicable to the administration of the county's annual audit process.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
269:
In conjunction with the preparation of the annual financial report addressed in section 3-44, the county shall, pursuant to requirements impose by Georgia law, provide for and cause to be made an annual audit of its financial affairs and transactions of all funds and activities of the local government for each of its fiscal years.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
270:
(a) The performing auditor shall be a properly licensed independent certified public accounting (CPA) firm.
(b) The CPA firm must have experience in auditing Georgia local governments to be considered for the role of performing auditor.
(c) Proposals shall be sought from as many qualifying firms as may be interested in the opportunity, with invitations to propose to be sent to a minimum of three CPA firms.
(d) The chairperson shall recommend the CPA firm to serve as the performing auditor to the board of commissioners and shall provide copies of the proposals submitted by all proposing CPA firms to the board of commissioners.
(e) The board of commissioners shall on or before the final day of the month following the end of each fiscal year retain the performing auditor.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
271:
During the third year of the audit services relationship with a performing auditor, the county shall issue a request for proposal to choose its performing auditor for the following three years, with the current performing auditor to be allowed to submit a proposal for the following new three-year audit.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
272:
(a) All financial statements and schedules in the annual financial report shall be audited by the performing auditor.
(b) The audit shall be conducted in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards (GAAS) and generally accepted governmental auditing standards (GAGAS).
(c) The county shall comply with the requirements of the general accounting office (GAO) and the office of management and budget (OMB) when audits are conducted relating to federal funding, consistent with the 1996 (and any future) amendments to the Single Audit Act.
(d) The performing auditor's opinions must be included in the annual audit report.
(e) The county shall provide a copy of each annual audit report within 180 days after the close of its applicable fiscal year to the state auditor in accordance with Georgia law.
(f) The county shall provide written comments on the findings and recommendations in the audit report, including a plan for corrective action taken or planned and comments on the status of corrective action taken on prior findings and a copy of each annual financial report within 180 days after the close of its applicable fiscal year in accordance with Georgia law.
(g) The performing auditor shall transmit to the grand jury of the Superior Court of Pickens County a copy of each annual report furnished by said accountant to the board of commissioners.
(h) The county shall file each annual audit report with the Carl Vinson Institute of Government of the University of Georgia concurrent with submission it to the state auditor in accordance with Georgia law.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
275:
This article shall be applicable to the institution of the county's protocols for procurements, which shall be accomplished in accordance with Georgia law and with the provisions contained herein.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
276:
(a) These procurements protocols shall be applicable to the conducting of procurements made by the following parties operating under the span-of-control of the board of commissioners and for purposes of this article which are referred to collectively as the "Procuring parties" and individually as "a procuring party":
(1) The board of commissioners acting on the whole as such.
(2) The chairperson.
(3) A district commissioner acting in his or her individual capacity as a commissioner.
(4) The departments operating under the direct control of the chairperson ("county departments").
(b) The employees of the county departments who are authorized by this article or the chairperson to be involved in the conducting of procurements.
(c) Procurements mean acquisitions of real property, personal property, goods, materials, supplies and services by the procuring parties or a procuring party which include:
(1) Purchases, lease-purchases and leases of real property, personal property, goods, materials, supplies and other similar items.
(2) Purchases of services.
Note: These acquisitions are referred to generally hereinafter in this article as "procurement" in the singular or "procurements" in the plural.
(d) The following acquisitions shall not be considered as procurements subject to this article and, accordingly, shall not be subject to its protocols:
(1) Acquisitions involving public works construction shall be made in compliance with O.C.G.A. tit. 36, ch. 91 transactions in situations where the provisions therein are applicable to a given acquisition.
(2) Acquisitions involving road construction which shall be made in compliance with O.C.G.A. tit. 32, ch. 4, art. 3 in situations where the provisions therein are applicable a given acquisition.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
277:
In addition to the requirements set forth in the balance of this article, the conducting of procurements by procuring parties or a procuring party shall be fully performed in accordance with and subjected to all applicable Georgia and local laws and regulations related to ethics and ethical standards of conduct. (See the article VI, entitled "Code of Ethics", in chapter 2 of the Code.)
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
278:
(a) It shall be considered a "breach of duty" on the part of procuring parties or a procuring party who fails to follow the protocols set forth in this article.
(b) It shall also be considered a "breach of duty" on the part of procuring parties or a procuring party who conducts a procurement but is not authorized by this article or the chairperson to be involved in the conducting of procurements.
(c) The county will not be responsible for any procurement made as the result of such a breach of duty.
(d) At the direction of the board of commissioners upon a recommendation by the chairperson, the costs of any such noncompliant procurement shall be administratively considered to be the personal liability of the procuring parties or a procuring party who failed to adhere to the required procurement protocols.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
279:
(a) The conducting of procurements shall be subject to the levels-of-approval requirements set forth in this section, unless designated as a special procurement category in section 3-189 with that section setting forth the protocols governing the conducting of special procurements.
(b) The board of commissioners must approve any procurement with a value greater than $75,000.00.
Any change order to an agreement resulting from the prior approval of a procurement by the board of commissioners shall also require approval by the board of commissioners prior to the commencement of the subject change.
(c) Except for procurements addressed in subsection (f), the chairperson must approve any procurement with a value exceeding $10,000.00 and up to and including $75,000.00.
(1) Any change order to an agreement resulting from the prior approval of a procurement by the chairperson shall also require approval by the chairperson prior to the commencement of the subject change.
(2) Any change order to an agreement resulting from the prior approval of a procurement by the chairperson that causes the accumulated value of the item or service acquired to exceed $75,000.00 must be approved by the board of commissioners prior to the commencement of the subject change.
(d) Except for procurements addressed in subsection (f), the applicable head of county department ("department head") may approve any procurement with a value up to and including $10,000.00.
(1) Any change order to an agreement resulting from the prior approval of a procurement by a department head that causes the accumulated value of the item or service acquired to exceed $10,000.00 must be approved by the chairperson prior to the commencement of the subject change.
(2) Any change order to an agreement resulting from the prior approval of a procurement by a department head that causes the accumulated value of the item or service acquired to exceed $75,000.00 must be approved by the board of commissioners.
(e) Under no circumstances shall any procurement be arbitrarily segmented to circumvent the level-of-approval requirements mandated by this section.
(f) Notwithstanding the previous subsections (b), (c), (d) and (e) of this section, the board of commissioners must approve any procurement that involves an agreement that has a term of more than one year.
(1) Any such approved multiyear procurement shall require the execution of a written procurement agreement by the chairperson.
(2) The county's funds must be available to meet the county's payment obligations pursuant to the multiyear procurement agreement for the first fiscal period at the time of its execution by the chairperson.
(3) The county's payment and performance obligations pursuant to the multiyear procurement agreement for succeeding fiscal periods shall be contingent on the availability and appropriation of the county's funds.
(4) The term of the multiyear procurement agreement and the conditions of its renewal or extension, if any, must be included in the solicitation of the procurement.
(5) The multi-year procurement agreement shall comply with all applicable requirements imposed by Georgia law.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
282:
(a) In the discretion of the board of commissioners, procurements with a value of $75,000.00 or more may be made pursuant to Georgia statewide procurement contracts through the Georgia Department of Administrative Services in lieu of obtaining sealed bids or competitive proposals when doing so is to the clear advantage of the county.
In the discretion of the board of commissioners, procurements with a value of $75,000.00 or more may be made pursuant to any other viable government procurement contracts or any viable government procurement cooperatives in lieu of obtaining sealed bids or competitive proposals provided that any such other government procurement contract or government procurement cooperative has been successfully utilized by another Georgia county or a Georgia municipality to successfully complete a procurement with a value of $100,000.00 or more.
(b) In the discretion of the chairperson, procurements with a value exceeding $5,000.00 up to $75,000.00 may be made pursuant to Georgia statewide procurement contracts through the Georgia Department of Administrative Services in lieu of obtaining competitive proposals when doing so is to the clear advantage of the county.
At the discretion of the chairperson, procurements with a value exceeding $5,000.00 up to $75,000.00 may be made pursuant to any other viable government procurement contract or any viable government procurement cooperative in lieu of obtaining competitive proposals, provided that such other government procurement contract or government procurement cooperatives has been successfully utilized by another Georgia county or a Georgia municipality to successfully complete a procurement of $100,000.00 or more.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
283:
Each procurement within one of the following special procurement categories shall be subject to the procurement protocols specifically applicable to it and thereby exempt from the requirements set forth in sections 3-186 and section 3-187.
(a) Procurements of real property, including related services and other related items, as addressed in section 3-190.
(b) Retentions of professional services providers to procure certain professional services, as addressed in section 3-191.

(d) Procurements of utilities (e.g., electricity, gas, water, fuel, cable and telephone) as addressed in section 3-193.
(e) Travel expenditures incurred in the normal course of conducting county business, as addressed in section 3-194.
The chairperson may direct that a competitive procurement be conducted regarding any of the aforesaid special procurement categories when deemed appropriate and in the best interest of the county.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
284:
(a) Any procurement of real property, inclusive of real estate brokerage, abstracts of title for real property, title insurance for real property and other related costs of the procurement of the real property shall be approved by the board of commissioners.
(b) The procurement of real property shall require the execution of all required legal documents.
(c) Any agreements and legal documents related to the procurement of real property that require execution by the county must be executed by the chairperson, with such execution requiring prior authorization by the board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
285:
(a) The retention of any professional services provider for the purposes of procuring legal, audit, engineering, architectural or information technology services shall require the approval of the board of commissioners.

(2) The retention by the board of commissioners of the county's auditor is subject to the additional requirements set forth in sections 3-163 and 3-164.
(b) The retention of any professional services provider for the purposes of procuring accounting, consulting and land surveying services shall require the approval of the chairperson.
Said retentions shall be conducted through the execution of professional services agreements or engagement letters, which must be executed by the chairperson.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
286:
(a) The chairperson may make or approve emergency procurements of supplies, materials, products, and services at his or her discretion in the event of an emergency which threatens health, welfare or safety of the public or of the county's employees and which requires immediate action.
(b) The chairperson shall prepare a written report documenting the need for any emergency procurement and the basis for selecting of the particular vendor.
Should the amount of any emergency procurement exceed $75,000.00, the chairperson shall provide the report to the board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
287:
(a) Procurements of electricity, gas, water, fuel, telephone and other utilities services shall require approval by the board of commissioners, upon recommendation by the chairperson.
(b) All such procurements must be conducted through written agreements, which must be executed by the chairperson, with such execution requiring prior authorization by the board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
288:
(a) The county shall pay or reimburse the chairperson, district commissioners and employees for expenditures incurred while traveling outside of Pickens County on official county business.
(b) The chairperson shall have prepared and shall maintain a policy document regulating the payments and reimbursements of said travel expenditures.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
289:
(a) Bonds or other security for procurement agreements and service procurement agreements may be required at the discretion of the chairperson on any procurement that he or she designates when doing so is determined to be a prudent measure to protect the county's interests.
(1) A bid bond or other bid security in the amount of a minimum of ten percent of the submitted bid or proposal quote may be required for procurements estimated to cost $20,000.00 or more.
Required bid bonds or other bid security shall be submitted at the time the bid or proposal for the procurement is submitted by prospective vendors and shall be retained by the county in the event that the awarded vendor selected fails to execute the procurement agreement awarded the county.
(2) A performance bond in an amount of up to 100 percent of the submitted bid or proposal quote may be required for procurements estimated to cost $5,000.00 or more.
Any required performance bond shall be submitted after the awarding of the procurement agreement and such performance bond may be called by the county in the event that the project is not completed by the awarded vendor in accordance with the procurement agreement.
(3) A payment bond in an amount of up to 100 percent of the submitted bid or proposal quote may be required for procurements estimated to cost $10,000.00 or more.
Any required payment bond shall be submitted after the awarding of the procurement agreement and any subcontractor or supplier of the awarded vendor may seek recovery against the payment bond in the event that the awarded vendor fails to make payments to that subcontractor or supplier.
(b) Any such bonding requirements shall be set forth in the solicitation of the sealed bid or competitive proposal for the procurement.
(c) Required bonds can take the form of cash, certified check, irrevocable letter of credit or an insurance product from a surety company in good standing with the office of the Georgia Insurance and Fire Safety Commissioner.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
290:
(a) Requests for a procurement shall originate in the county department requiring the products or services. Each respective department head or designee shall ensure budget appropriation is adequate. If insufficient funding exist, budget adjustment procedures shall be followed pursuant to section 3-78 and 3-79.
(b) The department head shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with all procedural requirements regarding all procurements when budget appropriations are available.
(c) Procurements shall not be considered to be approved until signed by the appropriate approving party pursuant to section 3-185. after the satisfaction of all procurement requirements set forth in this article.
(d) Procurement requests shall be made in the form of purchase orders through the county's administrative management system, except for:
(1) Procurements totaling $500.00 or less;
(2) Procurements made pursuant to written agreements (e.g., payments made for real property purchases, professional services, insurance, technical services and utilities); Written agreements and contracts for services shall be signed by the chairperson.
(3) Postage;
(4) Employee payroll, benefits and employee tax payments; and
(5) Travel expenditures.
(e) Purchase orders must be completed prior to submission through the county's administrative management system for approval.
(f) An addition to or an amendment of an original purchase order requiring additional products, services and/or charges shall be approved by the appropriate approving party pursuant to section 3-185.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
293:
(a) This article shall be applicable to the management all the county's financial assets.
(b) Financial assets include the county's cash on-hand, checks, deposited funds and lawful investments.
(c) The management of the county's pension fund assets held by a third-party custodian is not subject to this article.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
294:
(a) The chairperson, the district commissioners or any county employees involved in the investment process shall refrain from personal business activity that could conflict with proper execution of the investment program, or which could impair their ability to make impartial investment decisions.
(b) Potential conflicts of interest shall be disclosed to the board of commissioners immediately on applicable party's becoming aware of the potential conflict of interest.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
295:
All of the county's financial assets shall be managed in accordance with four principles listed in order of importance.
(a) Protecting the principal investment or corpus of the financial assets.
(b) Sustaining liquidity.
(c) Maintaining the diversification of the portfolio of financial assets.
(d) Attaining a market rate of return on the financial assets.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
296:
(a) The county's investments, other than those utilizing unexpended bond proceeds, shall be made solely in instruments permitted by O.C.G.A. § 36-83-4.
(b) The county's investments utilizing unexpended bond proceeds shall be made solely in instruments permitted by O.C.G.A. § 36-82-7.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
297:
Decisions concerning financial assets involving a placement or investment must be made by the board of commissioners upon consideration of a recommendation of the chairperson.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
298:
(a) All investment securities purchased by the county shall be held in safekeeping by an institution designated as primary agent.
(b) The primary agent shall issue a safekeeping receipt to the county listing the specific instrument, rate, maturity and other pertinent information.
(c) The county shall require pledges of collateral from the depository institution covering at least 110 percent of the investment in accordance with Georgia law.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
299:
(a) Cash and or checks collected by county departments shall be provided to the finance department on the following business today after receipt.
(b) Deposits of cash and checks shall be made by the finance department bi-weekly.
(c) All cash and checks shall be kept in a secure location prior to deposits being made.
(d) The county shall require pledges of collateral from the depository institution covering at least 110 percent of the deposits is in accordance with Georgia law.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
302:
(a) This article shall be applicable to the undertaking and management of county debt, which for purposes of this article the term "undertaking of debt by the county" shall include:
(1) The direct incurrence of debt by the county.
(2) The guaranteeing in of another party's debt by the county any manner and by any means.
(3) Payments made to another party that have the direct effect or indirect effect of subsidizing that party's servicing of its debt.
(b) Debt shall include bonds, notes and capital leases.
(c) The county shall fully comply with federal and Georgia law in all aspects involved in the undertaking of debt.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
303:
(a) The county shall seek to procure items and cover expenditures by means other than by the undertaking of debt.
(b) The county shall only guarantee the debt of another party in situations that have a compelling public interest and that that cannot otherwise be served as determined on the basis of the most prudent deliberation by the board of commissioners as a matter of public record.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
304:
(a) The county shall only undertake long-term debt when doing so is necessary to fulfill a compelling public need. The county shall not undertake long term debt to fund current operations.
(b) When undertaking long-term debt to fulfill a compelling public need, the county shall take all steps necessary to obtain the most advantageous financing terms available in the market by exhaustively seeking competing proposals from at least three different financial institutions.
(c) The county shall not undertake debt with a variable-rate structure except in the most fiscally prudent and responsible manner based on the most careful review possible.
(d) Any long-term debt term debt incurred by the county shall be obtained in strict conformity with the provisions of Georgia law governing its issuance.
(e) The term of any long-term debt shall not exceed the useful life of the capital project, facility or equipment for which the borrowing is intended.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
305:
The county shall adhere to the following conditions when the board of commissioners finds it necessary to undertake debt by issuing general obligation bonds.
(a) Financing from general obligation bonds shall be confined to projects which cannot otherwise be financed from current revenues.
(b) Bonds shall only be issued on a competitive basis.
(1) A minimum of three financial institutions shall be considered by the board of commissioners for each general obligation bond.
(2) This requirement is not applicable if proposals are not received from three financial institutions after an exhaustive effort is exerted to obtain a minimum of three proposals.
(3) This subsection is not applicable when the lender is a federal agency or a Georgia agency.
(c) Bonds shall be structured to allow level debt service, with principal being reduced each year.
(d) Annual debt service expenditures for all general obligation bonds shall not exceed ten percent of the combination of annual general fund revenues and the amount of annual SPLOST funds specifically designated to fund general obligation bonds.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
306:
The county shall adhere to the following conditions when the board of commissioners finds it necessary to undertake debt by issuing revenue bonds.
(a) The county shall issue revenue bonds only in the most fiscally prudent and responsible manner pursuant to the most careful reviews possible.
(1) Prudent projections of revenue expected from the revenue producing project being financed by a particular revenue bond must fully justify the issuance of the revenue bond.
(2) A comprehensive risk assessment of the revenue producing project must be conducted to justify the issuance of the revenue bond.
(b) Financing from revenue bonds shall be confined to projects which cannot otherwise be financed from current revenues.
(c) Revenue bonds shall only be issued on a competitive basis.
(1) A minimum of three financial institutions shall be considered by the board of commissioners for each revenue bond.
(2) This requirement is not applicable if proposals are not received from three financial institutions after an exhaustive effort is exerted to obtain a minimum of three proposals.
(d) Bonds shall be structured to allow level debt service, with principal being reduced each year.
If deemed appropriate, the county may use a wrap-around debt service structure to match the anticipated revenue derived from the underlying security of bonds.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
307:
(a) The amount of long-term debt financing for the procurement of capital assets through capital leases may be up to 100 percent of the fair market value of the assets.
(b) The requirements imposed by article VIII shall be met in order in order for the county to enter into a capital lease.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
308:
(a) Any decision by the board of commissioners to conditionally obligate the county to increase property taxes pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-5-220 for the purpose of guaranteeing debt undertaken by a third party to provide for financial assistance to county or joint county and municipal development authorities for the purpose of developing trade, commerce, industry, and employment opportunities shall be preceded by a public hearing on the matter.
(b) Said public hearing must occur no earlier than one month or no later than two weeks prior to the making of said decision.
(c) Advertisements for said public hearing shall be published for the for the two consecutive weeks in the official organ of Pickens County prior to the week of the public hearing.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
309:
(a) The county shall limit its short-term borrowing to cover cash flow shortages through a bank loan or the issuance of annual tax anticipation notes (TANs).
(b) TANs shall only be issued on a competitive basis.
(1) A minimum of three financial institutions shall be considered by the board of commissioners for each TAN.
(2) This requirement is not applicable if proposals are not received from three financial institutions after an exhaustive effort is exerted to obtain a minimum of three proposals.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))
310:
(a) When undertaking debt, the county shall comply with all applicable requirements imposed by federal law, including those regarding the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Internal Revenue Service.
(b) When undertaking debt, the county shall comply with all applicable requirements imposed by Georgia law.
(Ord. of 5-22-2025(2), § 1(Exh. A))

(c) Through this chapter 4 of the Code of Ordinances, Pickens County, Georgia ("chapter 4"), as adopted and amended pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 36-1-20 for the purpose of governing and policing of the unincorporated areas of Pickens County, the board of commissioners intends to ensure the most effective regulation possible of advertising and signs therein.
(d) The term, "Code", as used hereinafter in this chapter shall mean the Code of Ordinances, Pickens County, Georgia.
(Ord. of 5-5-2025(3), § 1(Exh. A))

Unincorporated areas. The provisions set forth in this chapter shall apply to the unincorporated areas of Pickens County and shall apply to and govern all land use intensity districts therein, as has been established or as will be established in the future by the board of commissioners pursuant to chapter 67 of the Code and no sign shall be erected or maintained in any land use intensity district unless it so done in strict compliance with this chapter.
(Ord. of 5-5-2025(3), § 1(Exh. A))
315:
The administration and enforcement of this chapter shall be conducted in strict and complete accordance with chapter 1 of the Code within the limitations imposed by O.C.G.A. § 36-1-20 and/or by other applicable general law.
(Ord. of 5-5-2025(3), § 1(Exh. A))
316:
(a) Operating within the span-of-control of the board of commissioners and under the direction of chairperson thereof, the Pickens County government shall administer and enforce the provisions of this chapter.

317:
(a) Violation. The term "violation" means:
(1) The performing of an act that is prohibited by any provision of this chapter; or
(2) The failing to perform an act that is required to be performed by any provision of this chapter.
(b) Person. The term, "person" means any individual, corporation, business trust, estate, trust, partnership, association, joint venture, utility, cooperative, or other legal or commercial entity.
(c) Person committing a violation. The term "person committing a violation" means a person committing a violation of this chapter.
(d) Penalties and punishment for a violation. A violation of any of the provisions of this chapter shall be punishable pursuant to chapter 1 of the Code and pursuant to this section by a fine not exceeding $1,000.00 or 60 days imprisonment, or both, except as otherwise prohibited by or as otherwise provided for by general law.
(e) Subsection (d) shall not preclude the imposition of higher penalties and punishment that are authorized to be imposed by general law.
(f) Continuing violations over an extended period of time.
(1) Each day that any violation of any provision of this chapter continues in sequence or occurs on separate nonsequential days shall constitute a separate violation, and each and every separate violation may accordingly be subjected to separate respective fines and/or imprisonment.
(2) Unless barred by limitations imposed by general law, there shall be no limit to the quantity of separate daily violations that can accumulate and be made by citation or by accusation in a given situation.
(3) The date of the first violation or of any subsequent violation subject to enforcement that occurs in any sequence of additional, separate daily violations, shall be deemed to be the earliest identifiable day on which the activity giving rise to the violation and shall be established on the basis of one or more applicable and sufficiently viable:
a. Documents;
b. Written or transcribed complaints;
c. Written or transcribed witness statements;
d. Recorded images;
e. Voice recordings.
(g) Violations by officers, agents and other associated individuals.
(1) Any violation of this chapter by any officer, agent or other associated individual acting for or employed by any corporation or unincorporated association or organization, while acting within the scope of his or her office or employment, shall in every case also be deemed to be a violation by such corporation, association, or organization.
(2) Any officer, agent or other associated individual acting for or employed by any corporation or unincorporated association or organization shall be subject and liable to punishment as well as the corporation or unincorporated association or organization for the violation by it of any provision of this chapter, where such violation was the act, omission or order, or the result of the act, omission or order, of any such officer, agent or other associated individual.
(h) Separate offenses for multiple persons involved in a violation. Each person who commits, participates in, or assists in the commission of any violation of any provision of this chapter may be found guilty of a separate offense related to that violation and may suffer the penalties provided herein for committing that violation; however, not more than one person may be subjected to penalties and punishment for any single violation.
(i) No bar to revocation or suspension.
(1) Any imposition of a fine and/or imprisonment pursuant to any provision of this chapter shall not prevent the revocation or the suspension of any license, permit, certificate, or franchise issued by any authorized county employee.
(2) Any imposition of a fine and/or imprisonment pursuant to any other provision of this chapter likewise shall not affect the issuance or continuation of any administrative order issued by any authorized county employee, including but not limited to, any stop-work order.
(j) Future amendments. The penalty provided by this section shall apply to the future amendment of any section of this chapter, whether or not such penalty is reenacted in the amendatory ordinance.
(k) Conflict with federal or state laws. If it is deemed by an applicable court of competent jurisdiction that a punishment imposed under this chapter conflicts with federal or state laws, the prevailing punishment shall be limited to the maximum permitted by law.
(Ord. of 5-5-2025(3), § 1(Exh. A))
